summary:
Bullpen and hitting ratings are carrying this model right now, and the board lines up perfectly with it tonight. All four ratings are flashing hot on bullpen_fatigue (+16.5pts R1-R3, +17.4pts R4) and bullpen (+11.1pts across R1-R3), while hitting is even hotter for R2 at +19.1pts over baseline (13-6, 68% last 14). The one red flag that cuts against all of it: SP is ice cold across the board, -21 to -23pts on every rating (R1-R4 all sitting at 6-13, 32% over the last 19 decisions). If tonight's pick leans on a starting-pitcher signal, fade that input hard — trust the pen and bat reads instead.

CLE @ TBR is the only game on the board, and it's about as clean a consensus as this model produces: all four ratings land on TBR, with R2 showing the strongest conviction at +1.65 delta — no surprise given R2's hitting cell is the hottest number on the sheet. TBR as a liked team has been excellent all year (43-19, 69%, n=62; strong plays 26-11, +21.0u), so the team-level history backs the rating convergence instead of fighting it. The catch is sample size: R3 and R4 strong plays have gone cold recently (R3 14d 2-1 but flat on units, R4 14d 0-2 for -2.0u), so don't let the unanimous call inflate confidence on bet sizing — lean on R1/R2, which are both riding 30-day stretches of 60%+ win rates and double-digit unit gains (R1 21-11 +12.0u, R2 19-11 +11.0u last 30). With SP cold and pen/hitting hot, a TBR play that's getting its signal from bullpen or hitting categories specifically is the sharpest version of tonight's pick — if the lean comes mostly from SP, trim stake accordingly.
